paper_title: Rethinking the Role of Prompting Strategies in LLM Test-Time Scaling A   Perspective of Probability Theory
caption: Results of combining adaptively scaling and dynamically choosing the optimal i on Phi-3.5-mini-Instruct on MATH.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The graph illustrates the relationship between sampling time and accuracy for various methods, comparing their performance on the MATH dataset using Phi-3.5-mini-Instruct.

The x-axis is labeled "Sampling Time" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and also has a linear scale, spanning from 40 to 75 in increments of 5.

The graph features seven distinct lines, each representing a different method: DiP (purple, triangle marker, solid line), AnP (orange, square marker, solid line), CoT (blue, triangle marker, solid line), L2M (cyan, triangle marker, solid line), SBP (peach, square marker, solid line), Dynamic w/ Oracle (black, square marker, dashed line), and Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle (red, circle marker, dashed line). 

DiP starts at around 45 accuracy at a sampling time of 0 and gradually increases to approximately 50 by a sampling time of 70. AnP begins at around 40 accuracy and rises to about 55 by a sampling time of 30, remaining relatively stable thereafter. CoT starts at roughly 42 accuracy and reaches around 55 by a sampling time of 20, with minor fluctuations. L2M begins at approximately 43 accuracy and increases to about 55 by a sampling time of 20. SBP starts at around 40 accuracy and rises to approximately 54 by a sampling time of 30. Dynamic w/ Oracle commences at around 68 accuracy and gradually increases to about 70 by a sampling time of 70. Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle begins at roughly 69 accuracy and ascends to approximately 77 by a sampling time of 20, remaining relatively stable thereafter. Notably, Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle consistently outperforms all other methods across the entire sampling time range.

Overall, the graph effectively compares the performance of different methods in terms of accuracy over varying sampling times, highlighting the superior performance of Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle.

The x-axis, labeled "Sampling Time," is linearly scaled, spanning from 0 to 70 with tick labels at intervals of 10. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linearly scaled, ranging from 40 to 75 with tick labels at intervals of 5. The diagram features seven distinct lines, each representing a different method: DiP (purple, solid line, triangle markers), AnP (orange, solid line, square markers), CoT (blue, solid line, triangle markers), L2M (cyan, solid line, square markers), SBP (peach, solid line, square markers), Dynamic w/ Oracle (black, dashed line, square markers), and Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle (red, dashed line, circle markers). The lines exhibit varying trends; DiP, AnP, CoT, L2M, and SBP show an initial increase in accuracy as sampling time increases from 0 to around 20-30, after which their accuracy stabilizes or slightly fluctuates, with values ranging from approximately 45 to 55. Dynamic w/ Oracle starts at an accuracy of around 68 at a sampling time of 0, increases to about 70 at a sampling time of 50, and remains stable thereafter. Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle begins at an accuracy of around 68 at a sampling time of 1, rises to approximately 77 at a sampling time of 30, and remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations at higher sampling times.
